about: The gate's lanes, read by scripts/gate_history.py's selection (docs/process.md, "Failure causes and the selection in shadow"). Declared by hand: jobs, needs, inputs, emission, evidence, always, physical, note; kept by `gate_history.py table --write`: first_seen, minutes, alone, defect_jobs, outside_jobs, history, shadow.

signatures.name: http-error-from-curl
signatures.pattern: curl: \(\d+\) (The requested URL returned error: (403|408|429|5\d\d)|Recv failure)
signatures.description: A curl download (pinned toolchain/tools) got an HTTP 403, 408, 429 or 5xx from the server or a connection reset.
signatures.example: curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer

signatures.name: fetch-http-error
signatures.pattern: (cannot fetch https?://\S+: HTTP (Error 5\d\d|status (403|5\d\d))|urllib\.error\.HTTPError: HTTP Error 5\d\d|pkg: Error: Unknown HTTP error)
signatures.description: landin_fetch/fetch_inputs python or FreeBSD pkg download got an HTTP 403/5xx (a 404 is excluded: pinned-file removals are real).

signatures.name: apt-mirror-failure
signatures.pattern: (E: Failed to fetch .*(Service Unavailable|Forbidden|Connection failed|unexpected size|timed out)|apt_install: .*out of time after \d+s|Could not connect to \S+:\d+ .*connection timed out)
signatures.description: An Ubuntu apt mirror answered 503/403, was out of sync (unexpected size), unreachable, or apt_install ran out of time.
signatures.example: apt_install: the image's mirrors: out of time after 396s

signatures.name: actions-download-429
signatures.pattern: Failed to download archive 'https://\S+' after \d+ attempts
signatures.description: The runner could not download an action tarball (codeload 429 rate limit) after retries; job fails before any step.

signatures.name: artifact-service-error
signatures.description: actions/upload-artifact could not reach/finish GitHub's artifact service (ENOTFOUND, 404).
signatures.example: ##[error]Failed to CreateArtifact: Unable to make request: ENOTFOUND

signatures.name: mac-homebrew-python-dyld
signatures.description: Self-hosted Mac's Homebrew python was upgraded under the toolchain installer (dyld missing library).

signatures.name: apt-dpkg-lock
signatures.pattern: Unable to acquire the dpkg frontend lock
signatures.description: Self-hosted runner: another apt-get holds the dpkg lock.
signatures.example: E: Unable to acquire the dpkg frontend lock (/var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend), is another process using it?

signatures.name: disk-full
signatures.pattern: (^error: disk full writing |^fatal error: disk full$|cp: error copying .*: No space left on device)
signatures.description: The runner ran out of disk (GNAT output write or nix store copy).

signatures.name: emacs-treesit-version-mismatch
signatures.pattern: Cannot activate tree-sitter, because language grammar for landin is unavailable \(version-mismatch\)
signatures.description: Self-hosted runner's Emacs tree-sitter library does not match the built grammar (editor-grammar lane).
signatures.example: Warning (treesit): Cannot activate tree-sitter, because language grammar for landin is unavailable (version-mismatch): 15

signatures.name: gprbuild-closed-pipe
signatures.description: gprbuild/gnat --version | head -1 wrote to a closed pipe (SIGPIPE ignored by host); a rerun passes.

signatures.name: probe-dmi-timeout
signatures.description: a RISC-V probe's debug-module access timed out, the maintainer's example; no run of the study met it

signatures.name: rig-probe-unreachable
signatures.pattern: probe at \S+ does not answer ping
signatures.description: The rig probe did not answer ping after a power cycle.
signatures.example: board failed: /run/github-runner/rigpi/_temp/board-leg/pico2/evidence/rp2350-boot: after the cycle the probe at 10.42.0.50 does not answer ping; stopping; resident image restoration pending: after the

signatures.name: rig-gpio-shell-timeout
signatures.pattern: probehive's lightweight GPIO shell, .* did not open within \d+ s
signatures.description: The probehive GPIO shell on the rig never opened (300 s timeout).
signatures.example: board failed: /run/github-runner/rigpi/_temp/board-leg/rp2040/evidence/rp2040-ram: probehive's lightweight GPIO shell, which gives scripts/gpio.py its LiteX, did not open within 300 s; prepare it with

signatures.name: rig-board-step-failed
signatures.description: A rig board step (RAM load, flash, resident-ready) failed through the probe on the physical rig.
signatures.example: board failed: /run/github-runner/rigpi/_temp/board-leg/rp2040/evidence/rp2040-boot: flash failed (1); see /run/github-runner/rigpi/_temp/board-leg/rp2040/evidence/rp2040-boot/flash.log; resident image

signatures.name: rig-board-readback-glitch
signatures.pattern: (\d+ bytes? had arrived when the boot frame was written|waited \d+ s for the boot frame; received \d+ bytes?|recoveries reads? \d+ over JTAG, \d+ in the frame|esp32c3 ram: the unhandled entry took \d+ trap)
signatures.description: A board harness read-back glitch on the rig: stray UART bytes before the stm32h753 boot frame, esp32c3 JTAG counter skew, or a spurious trap at boot. Passes on rerun.
signatures.example: boards esp32c3: failed: esp32c3 ram: the unhandled entry took 1 trap(s), the last mcause 0x0 at 0x0, mtval 0x0, sp 0x3fcc7c90

signatures.name: board-console-first-echo-race
signatures.pattern: stm32h753 ram: the shared scenario was not echoed
signatures.description: stm32h753 console first-echo race in the board harness; passes on rerun.
signatures.example: boards stm32h753: failed: stm32h753 ram: the shared scenario was not echoed

signatures.name: emulator-guest-banner-timeout
signatures.pattern: Connection timed out during banner exchange
signatures.description: FreeBSD VM guest ssh connection timed out during banner exchange.
signatures.example: Connection timed out during banner exchange

signatures.name: stale-ubuntu-qemu-8
signatures.description: Ubuntu QEMU 8.2 user emulation in the job (known-bad sigaction size); failures in that lane are the emulator, not the code. Condition, not error line.

documents.note: check.py over every document, grammar table and generated page; full history checkout.

scripts.note: scripts/script_tests.py (every scripts/tests module and check.py's controls), actionlint, determinism/quality/debugging controls.

linux-debug-build.note: Debug refine and test program on Linux x86-64, packaged for the debug lanes.

compiler.note: scripts/test.sh --shard=I/4 with the debug compiler: the whole Ada test program and fixture corpus. Compiles negatives, unit tests and everything else, not only positives.

compiler-checks.note: Emacs lsp, determinism closures, native report identity, publication/cancellation, server sessions and the mutation fuzzer with the debug compiler.

linux-release-build.note: Release refine over the cached object tree; the compiler every later Linux lane takes.

linux-release-clean.note: Release refine from clean; consumed only by linux-release-compare.

linux-release-compare.note: Cached and clean release builds must be byte-identical (compare_builds.py).

release.note: Release compiler: full corpus, verifier resources, closures/server, installed toolchain outside the checkout, install script, static archive on Alpine, object quality, GDB and DAP sessions.

outside-user-stock.note: Packaged release compiler used from outside the checkout on stock Ubuntu, plus the user container image.

build-modes.note: emit_manifest.py modes --shard=I/4: debug and release compilers must emit identical bytes for positive+runtime+Cortex-M corpora at the standard profiles.

bindings.note: refine bindings against the pinned Clang with the debug compiler; regenerates the committed fixture byte for byte.

editor-grammar.note: Tree-sitter grammar parses every positive/runtime/abi fixture and core; committed parser regenerates; Neovim smoke. Uses no compiler.

flake-compiler.note: nix build .#refine and .#refine-bin, flake check over all systems, dev shell, README nix route. The flake source is the whole tree (version read from README.md); listed paths are what its build and checks read.

measure-size.note: Code size of every measured workload at every level/profile for Linux, RV64, Windows and firmware targets, linked by nix-pinned linkers, held to the base commit's baselines; plus RV64 instruction counts.

cortex-m-programs.note: Cortex-M part 'programs' on locked QEMU/GDB: probe controls, M0 instruction counts vs baselines, devices from SVD, every board port built offline, lanes abi/memory/packed/etc.

cortex-m-corpus.note: Cortex-M part 'corpus': the freestanding runtime/abi corpus on the Arm lanes under QEMU.

cortex-m-rv32.note: Cortex-M harness part 'rv32': RV32 controls and corpora on Espressif's QEMU.

xtensa-esp32.note: Xtensa esp32: native controls (shard 1) and one third of the complete freestanding corpus under Espressif's QEMU. Compiles runtime/abi fixtures and hand-written control programs.

xtensa-esp32s3.note: Xtensa esp32s3: native controls (shard 1) and one third of the complete freestanding corpus under Espressif's QEMU. Compiles runtime/abi fixtures and hand-written control programs.

scaling.note: Generated 1k-16k declaration programs checked and emitted with the release compiler; doubling time ratio bound.

darwin-release-build.note: Release refine on macOS over the cached object tree (ZERO_AR_DATE).

darwin-release-clean.note: Release refine on macOS from clean; consumed only by darwin-release-compare.

darwin-release-compare.note: Cached and clean macOS release builds must be byte-identical.

darwin-debug-build.note: Debug refine and test program on macOS.

darwin-host.note: test.sh --host --target=linux-x86-64 --shard=I/4 on a Mac with the debug compiler, plus closures, publication/cancellation and server sessions.

darwin-host-release.note: Release-compiler host suite on a Mac (2 shards), Darwin sizes vs baselines, installed toolchain, install script, LLDB sessions and DAP over lldb-dap.

darwin-parity.note: Native execution of the shared runtime/abi corpus (check.py --parity), source verdicts for positives and negatives (diagnostics.py) and bindings archives. Runs runtime, negative and abi fixtures.

arm64-compiler.note: scripts/test.sh --shard=I/3 on arm64 with the debug compiler.

arm64-compiler-checks.note: arm64 debug compiler: verifier observations, default target, determinism closures, publication/cancellation, server sessions.

arm64-release.note: Full test.sh corpus on arm64 with the release compiler.

arm64-release-checks.note: arm64 release: default target/server, installed toolchain, install script, static archive on Alpine, user image, GDB and DAP sessions, AAPCS64 bindings against pinned Clang.

freebsd-amd64-runtime.note: Linux-built FreeBSD x86-64 runtime corpus emitted, booted and executed in a QEMU guest.

freebsd-amd64-debugger.note: FreeBSD x86-64 LLDB debugger sessions in the guest.

freebsd-amd64-abi.note: FreeBSD x86-64 ABI fixtures with their C peers in the guest.

freebsd-arm64-runtime.note: FreeBSD arm64 runtime corpus in two shards (--shard=I/2) in a QEMU guest.

freebsd-arm64-debugger.note: FreeBSD arm64 LLDB debugger sessions in the guest.

freebsd-arm64-abi.note: FreeBSD arm64 ABI fixtures with their C peers in the guest.

freebsd-amd64-size.note: FreeBSD x86-64 section sizes of the measured workloads vs baselines.

freebsd-arm64-size.note: FreeBSD arm64 section sizes of the measured workloads vs baselines.

freebsd-toolchain.note: Restore or build the pinned GNAT/GPRbuild for FreeBSD x86-64 (cache or a guest build).

freebsd-host.note: refine built in a FreeBSD x86-64 guest and the Ada test program run there in two shards (git bundle of the whole tree).

freebsd-host-release.note: Release build and package archive made and smoke-tested in the FreeBSD guest.

windows-emit.note: Linux release compiler emits the Windows x86-64 runtime/abi/Microsoft-link/debugger bundles; NativeWindowsLink unit tests.

windows-runtime.note: Windows runner executes the x86-64 corpus bundle and the ABI fixtures with C peers. Verdict is a function of windows-emit's bundle plus the harness, but the bundle comes from runtime/abi fixtures, so compiler inputs are listed.

windows-microsoft.note: Windows runner links the x86-64 bundle with Microsoft's link.exe and executes it.

windows-debugger.note: Windows LLDB sessions over images and PDBs, and a refine dap session from WSL.

windows-arm64-emit.note: As windows-emit for windows-arm64 (llvm-mingw arm64 import libraries).

windows-arm64-runtime.note: Windows 11 arm64 runner executes the arm64 corpus and ABI fixtures.

windows-arm64-microsoft.note: Windows 11 arm64 runner links with Microsoft's arm64 linker and executes.

windows-arm64-debugger.note: Windows arm64 LLDB sessions and a refine dap session from WSL 1 over the arm64 release compiler.

rv64-qemu.note: test.sh --target=linux-rv64 --runner=qemu-riscv64 --shard=I/2 under the pinned QEMU user emulation; shard 1 also RV64 GDB and DAP sessions.

determinism / manifest (x86_64-linux).note: emit_manifest.py emit --shard=I/4: this host's debug compiler emits assembly digests of every positive fixture on all 11 targets, 9 profiles, both modes. Output consumed only by agree. Workflow-level needs name all three debug builds.

determinism / manifest (aarch64-linux).note: emit_manifest.py emit --shard=I/3: this host's debug compiler emits assembly digests of every positive fixture on all 11 targets, 9 profiles, both modes. Output consumed only by agree. Workflow-level needs name all three debug builds.

determinism / manifest (aarch64-darwin).note: emit_manifest.py emit --shard=I/4: this host's debug compiler emits assembly digests of every positive fixture on all 11 targets, 9 profiles, both modes. Output consumed only by agree. Workflow-level needs name all three debug builds.

determinism / agree.note: Merges each host's shards and requires every host's manifest to agree (emit_manifest.py compare).

board-bundles.note: Release compiler builds every board's boot and RAM bundles strict against the hardware records (and timing images on a timed event); one artifact with provenance.

board.note: One leg per port on the rig runner: RAM and boot runs on hardware (and timing runs on a timed event). Checkout is sparse to these roots.

measure-time.note: Paired wall-time of candidate vs base compiler's images on each native runner; schedule and dispatch only.
